Use case: precise-object-edit.
EDIT the supplied single metatarsal segment. Current LOWER END looks like a large bulb and fails the ankle-to-toe attachment.
Change only its LOWER THIRD: the width must progressively taper downward to a SMALL smoothly convex distal end. The very bottom endpoint width must be about 40 to 45 percent of the widest upper part, and must NEVER expand into a ball or club. Lower-third silhouette continues narrower than middle all the way down. Small rounded seam overlap is enough; no flat cut, no spike, no foot/toes. Reduce the lower terminal swelling aggressively.
Preserve the upper two thirds' silhouette, material, scale rows, lighting, bronze-brown/olive colors and pale right underside as closely as possible. Keep one complete upright side-view cutout with the same generous margins and true transparent alpha; no new pieces, background, shadow, text or mechanical joints.
The top broad end still belongs at the ankle behind the tibia; the narrow bottom must join a thin low toe root. This is one compact load-bearing METATARSAL part, not a knee or shin.
